newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy open to international action on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Italy open to international action on Zaire.

text.p: Italy will consider supporting any international action in Zaire which should focus on securing an airport to ensure humanitarian aid gets through, Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said on Monday.
Andreatta told reporters that although Italy was not "the best-placed country to undertake an initiative" it was willing to look into the possibility of taking part.
"There are no reasons of principle that could lead us to not look into the possibility of taking part," he said.

"France and Belgium, for their ties and above all their knowledge of the area, can evaluate better than us the prospects of an intervention that can only be to defend some airport to allow the flow of humanitarian aid," Andreatta said.
The minister ruled out the sending of forces to act as peacekeepers between the warring sides.
"What could be done, if necessary, is to guarantee food supplies for refugees between Zaire and Rwanda," Andreatta said, adding that "it might be opportune to guarantee it militarily".
The French military has said mounting a humanitarian operation to save refugees in eastern Zaire is feasible, but Paris first wants a clear international mandate.
Italy said on Saturday that "suitable measures of protection" were needed so the United Nations could aid refugees in eastern Zaire.
A French cabinet minister urged European partners on Sunday to be prepared to intervene to prevent a human disaster threatening more than one million refugees in Kivu province.

Officials said the French government was waiting to see whether African heads of state, due to discuss the Zaire fighting at a meeting in Nairobi on Tuesday, would call for action by the European Union.
The Italian Foreign Ministry said on Sunday that Italy was backing the Kenyan-led initiative.
It said Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini had asked Italy's representatives in Kinshasa and Kigali to urge the governments concerned to accept the Kenyan mediation.
The ministry also said that it had a plane full of medicines, food and clothing on standby to fly to the city of Goma in eastern Zaire as soon as the airport was secure.
